filing.text_data: Public libraries -and the communities they serve- NEED E-Rate! Please ensure continued funding for this vital economic program. Especially in rural areas where internet access is scarce and often unaffordable, this program provides access for citizens to get work, file taxes, find housing, acquire degrees or certifications, submit required documentation and paperwork, etc. Cutting off or limiting E-Rate funding limits how community members may contribute to society and support themselves. Public internet access encourages full economic participation and should be supported at all governmental levels.

filing.text_data:
As a drone hobbyist, I am have doubts about this ruling that is about to be enforced.  I have one simple question:  do you have actual proof that DJI products are transmitting data to China?  If so, share it us.  We have yet to see this and we can't just accept your word.  I would like tangible, indisputable proof that this is truly an issue.

Even if the 8 companies in question have ties to DJI, they are making a superior consumer product as right now, we hobbyists have zero options.  Is that the endgame to take hobbyists out of the picture?  

It is imperative that the FCC doesn't blindly make this decision based on unfounded facts regarding the transmission of data.  Please reconsider this ruling and think of the millions of hobbyists as well as small business owners that will be adversely impacted.

Thank you,
Michael Lowe

filing.text_data:
Elite Fund, Inc. appreciates this opportunity to submit comments in response to the Commission’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) and Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (FNPRM). 
E-Rate is a critical program that helps schools and libraries provide reliable, affordable connectivity for students, staff, and the communities they serve.
One customer story I have is a school in Benton Harbor, MI that until 2020, they were only able to get a T-1 (1.5Mbps) for their Internet services for all 130 students and numerous staff. Because of  the E-rate grant, they were able to get 40% covered on the fiber build out to their school. That build was almost $23,000. They now enjoy a 500Mbps fiber connection, which has greatly helped with their online testing and educational needs. Another story for several of my customers is that E-rate helps to pay for network equipment that is greatly needed and very expensive. One switch can cost over $5,000. Without E-rate help, my schools and libraries would not be able to afford the necessary infrastructure needed to educate students and patrons.
Without this funding, there are absolutely no positives to cutting E-rate funding. Schools and libraries cannot afford the necessary equipment needed to educate their students and patrons. It would be a huge hit to their budgets. A lot of times, the 5-year Category 2 budget isn't enough to cover the necessary 5-year replacement of switches and access points, let alone the other needed equipment such as firewalls and cabling. And even though Internet prices have come down over the years, it can still be expensive. Schools and libraries depend on the E-rate grant to help supplement their already constrained budgets.
Elite Fund, Inc. respectfully urges the FCC to preserve E-Rate's core funding and support for schools and libraries, and to avoid changes that would reduce access or increase burden for the students and communities who depend on it.

filing.text_data: The FCC ordered early license reviews of eight ABC-owned stations in April (a process that wasn't supposed to begin until 2028) and is also investigating daytime talk show "The View" over federal rules about airtime for political candidates. Both actions came after President Trump directly pressured regulators to punish broadcasters he says treat him unfairly. ABC has called the license reviews "unlawful, arbitrary, and unconstitutional."  It is a clear violation of the First Amendment to the Constitution that guarantees freedom of speech.  These are not "official acts" as defined by the Supreme Court and I hope all involved in these types of unlawful actions are held to account.
